pragma solidity ^0.8.0;
// OpenZeppelin Contracts v4.4.1 (token/ERC20/extensions/IERC20Permit.sol)

/**
 * @dev Interface of the ERC20 Permit extension allowing approvals to be made via signatures, as defined in
 * https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2612[EIP-2612].
 *
 * Adds the {permit} method, which can be used to change an account's ERC20 allowance (see {IERC20-allowance}) by
 * presenting a message signed by the account. By not relying on {IERC20-approve}, the token holder account doesn't
 * need to send a transaction, and thus is not required to hold Ether at all.
 */
interface IERC20Permit {
  /**
   * @dev Sets `value` as the allowance of `spender` over ``owner``'s tokens,
   * given ``owner``'s signed approval.
   *
   * IMPORTANT: The same issues {IERC20-approve} has related to transaction
   * ordering also apply here.
   *
   * Emits an {Approval} event.
   *
   * Requirements:
   *
   * - `spender` cannot be the zero address.
   * - `deadline` must be a timestamp in the future.
   * - `v`, `r` and `s` must be a valid `secp256k1` signature from `owner`
   * over the EIP712-formatted function arguments.
   * - the signature must use ``owner``'s current nonce (see {nonces}).
   *
   * For more information on the signature format, see the
   * https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2612#specification[relevant EIP
   * section].
   */
  function permit(
    address owner,
    address spender,
    uint256 value,
    uint256 deadline,
    uint8 v,
    bytes32 r,
    bytes32 s
  ) external;

  /**
   * @dev Returns the current nonce for `owner`. This value must be
   * included whenever a signature is generated for {permit}.
   *
   * Every successful call to {permit} increases ``owner``'s nonce by one. This
   * prevents a signature from being used multiple times.
   */
  function nonces(address owner) external view returns (uint256);

  /**
   * @dev Returns the domain separator used in the encoding of the signature for {permit}, as defined by {EIP712}.
   */
  // solhint-disable-next-line func-name-mixedcase
  function DOMAIN_SEPARATOR() external view returns (bytes32);
}

Monad chain143 own Mento V3 Router only, not Celo-only v2, a bridged token, raw prefunded pair mint/swap, or an Aerodrome alias. The source acknowledges Aerodrome/Velodrome ancestry but the primary deployment is Mento FPMM FX infrastructure.

Exact-match MonadScan target Router source/ABI and constructor binding retained. Router is a direct constructor-based contract with immutable defaultFactory and factoryRegistry, no upgrade/admin/delegatecall or generic executor surface; approved factories and underlying oracle-priced pools remain mutable dependencies and are not independently admitted.

Ordinary calls pull caller ERC20 or LP tokens inside the same transaction; prior allowances/balances and an existing eligible pool are prerequisites, not granted here. Amounts are raw token units and LP liquidity units; output recipients can differ from caller. Minimum outputs are caller protections, not price or execution guarantees. Pool oracle validity, trading limits, market-hour breakers and fees may affect availability.

addLiquidity, removeLiquidity and swapExactTokensForTokens enforce a timestamp deadline. zapIn and zapOut have no deadline parameter; caller-specified swap minima and liquidity minima still apply. zapIn is payable in ABI but explicitly reverts for any nonzero msg.value; all selected methods require zero native value in practice.

Zaps use fixed Route/Zap financial structs and registry-approved factories, not opaque calldata/executor commands. They account using full router token balances and return full residual balances to caller; do not pre-fund the router or rely on unrelated residual balances. No claim/queue, bridge, permit, approval or new signing permission is admitted.
Pulls computed tokenA/tokenB amounts directly from caller to existing default-factory pool and mints LP to recipient within deadline/minima.

sourceSemantics.funding: addLiquidity pulls computed amounts from _msgSender() directly to pool, then mint(to). removeLiquidity pulls LP from _msgSender() to pool and burn(to). swapExactTokensForTokens quotes routes then pulls first input from _msgSender() to first pool before _swap with empty callback bytes; no separate public prefunding action.
sourceSemantics.ownership: No third-party payer input; normal caller is msg.sender since immutable trustedForwarder is zero. zapOut LP pull explicitly uses msg.sender; no signer/role/permit grant is selected.
sourceSemantics.recipients: LP add/zapIn mint to supplied to; remove and swap pay supplied to; zapOut returns assets to caller.
sourceSemantics.bounds: Three ordinary router methods ensure deadline. Zaps do not have deadlines; per-leg amountOutMin and liquidity amountAMin/amountBMin enforce minima. zapIn rejects nonzero msg.value although ABI payable.
sourceSemantics.routing: poolFor rejects factories not approved in immutable factoryRegistry; default factory selected on zero factory. Fixed Route fields select financial pools, no executable bytes. _swap calls only IRPool.swap with fixed amounts and empty callback data.
sourceSemantics.roundingAndResiduals: Liquidity token ratios use integer division; _addLiquidity requires existing default-factory pool. Zaps use full router token balances and return full residuals, so no per-caller persistent custody accounting is promised. Underlying FPMM decides LP mint/burn amounts and dynamic oracle/limit/fee behavior; dependency bytecode is not attested.

limitations: Static deployment/source/ABI metadata only: not live authorization, persistent runtime attestation, balances, liquidity, backing, financial safety, successful execution or a complete workflow. Existing independent grants, pauses, policies and canonical calldata/value controls remain mandatory.

Monad chain143 own Mento V3 Router only, not Celo-only v2, a bridged token, raw prefunded pair mint/swap, or an Aerodrome alias. The source acknowledges Aerodrome/Velodrome ancestry but the primary deployment is Mento FPMM FX infrastructure.

Exact-match MonadScan target Router source/ABI and constructor binding retained. Router is a direct constructor-based contract with immutable defaultFactory and factoryRegistry, no upgrade/admin/delegatecall or generic executor surface; approved factories and underlying oracle-priced pools remain mutable dependencies and are not independently admitted.

Ordinary calls pull caller ERC20 or LP tokens inside the same transaction; prior allowances/balances and an existing eligible pool are prerequisites, not granted here. Amounts are raw token units and LP liquidity units; output recipients can differ from caller. Minimum outputs are caller protections, not price or execution guarantees. Pool oracle validity, trading limits, market-hour breakers and fees may affect availability.

addLiquidity, removeLiquidity and swapExactTokensForTokens enforce a timestamp deadline. zapIn and zapOut have no deadline parameter; caller-specified swap minima and liquidity minima still apply. zapIn is payable in ABI but explicitly reverts for any nonzero msg.value; all selected methods require zero native value in practice.

Zaps use fixed Route/Zap financial structs and registry-approved factories, not opaque calldata/executor commands. They account using full router token balances and return full residual balances to caller; do not pre-fund the router or rely on unrelated residual balances. No claim/queue, bridge, permit, approval or new signing permission is admitted.
